title: Build a camera app with AVCam
abstract: Rebuild Apple's AVCam camera sample from an empty Xcode project, one chapter at a time, and learn how the iOS camera works.
footer: This site is an independent learning project. It is not an Apple product. AVCam is sample code from Apple.

chapters.title: First preview
chapters.abstract: The app asks for permission to use the camera and shows a live preview on the full screen. If the user denies the permission, the app shows a status message.

chapters.title: Cameras
chapters.abstract: A button changes between the back camera and the front camera with a blur transition. The app also follows the camera that the system prefers. A rotation coordinator keeps the preview level.

chapters.title: Take a photo
chapters.abstract: The capture button takes a photo and the screen flashes. The app logs the size of the photo data.

chapters.title: Save to Photos
chapters.abstract: Each photo goes to the Photos library together with its location. A thumbnail of the last photo appears, and a tap on it opens the photo picker.

chapters.title: Layout
chapters.abstract: The interface adapts to iPhone and iPad sizes, and the preview gets a viewfinder frame.

chapters.title: Focus and exposure
chapters.abstract: A tap on the preview sets the focus and the exposure at that point. The camera goes back to continuous mode when the scene changes.

chapters.title: Photo features
chapters.abstract: The app captures Live Photos and shows a "LIVE" badge. It also gets a quality prioritization picker, deferred photo delivery, and responsive capture.

chapters.title: Record video
chapters.abstract: A mode picker and a swipe change between photo and video. The app records movies with sound, shows the recording time, and saves each movie to Photos.

chapters.title: HDR video
chapters.abstract: An HDR button appears in video mode when the camera supports 10-bit HDR. The app then records HDR video.

chapters.title: A robust session
chapters.abstract: The app shows a message during an interruption and recovers from a media services reset. It starts fast, hides the controls until the session runs, and covers the old preview frame when it comes back from the background.

chapters.title: Hardware buttons and AirPods
chapters.abstract: The volume buttons, the Action button, the Camera Control, and a click on an AirPods stem capture media with the correct sounds. AirPods record high-quality audio.

chapters.title: Camera Control
chapters.abstract: The Camera Control shows zoom, exposure bias, and a custom slider for the lens position. The app interface becomes minimal while the control overlay is on the screen.

chapters.title: Lock Screen and Control Center
chapters.abstract: The app starts from the Lock Screen, Control Center, and the Action button through a capture extension and a control. The app and the extension share their state.

pages.title: Concepts: Lock Screen and Control Center
Build: Lock Screen and Control Center

chapters.title: Zoom and lenses
chapters.abstract: The app uses the back camera with the most lenses, shows zoom levels such as 0.5x, 1x, and 3x, and zooms with a pinch. This chapter goes beyond the Apple sample.

chapters.title: Fix the sample
chapters.abstract: You correct four defects of the Apple sample: a recording that ends by itself, the Live Photo badge, the rotation of a new movie connection, and a late capture sound.

chapters.title: iPhone Duo
chapters.abstract: On iPhone Duo, a camera can change the direction that it faces. The app follows the direction with a direction coordinator, mirrors the preview correctly, and centers its interface on the Duo display.
